messages:
incident-bot: URGENT: BGP route instability detected in GCP eu-west1 on interconnect-ics-01. Multiple prefixes are flapping; private-connectivity health checks failing for several Private deployments. Severity P2 — paging @net-oncall.
net-oncall: ack. pulling BGP state and router logs now. tagging as high priority.
ajay: seeing customer 5xx spike from 02:14 UTC for private endpoints in eu-west1, KV cache miss rate jumped 2% -> 28% for internal route-based caching. Impacting some on-prem overlapped networks.
marta: copying runbook (private-networking -> gcp-bgp-flap). first actions: 1) identify affected prefixes 2) consider local route dampening or withdraw 3) failover traffic to eu-west2 if stable.
sara: I'm on incident comms. prepping initial customer update. @net-oncall do we have a quick list of tenants behind affected prefixes?
net-oncall: quick grep from route-export shows: prefixes from 35.203.0.0/18 and 34.102.128.0/17 oscillating. correlating to tenants: AcmeCorp, Finlytics, MedData (private). sending CSV momentarily.
ops-bot: created incident ticket INC-2026-439 and attached initial alert bundle.
ajay: command outputs (from router):
```
# gcloud compute routers get-status rtr-ics-01 --region=europe-west1
state: BGP_NOT_ESTABLISHED
bgpPeers:
 - name: peer-onprem-1
   status: ESTABLISHED
 - name: peer-google-1
   status: ADJ-RIB-IN/ADJ-RIB-OUT flap
routes:
  received: 120
  accepted: 118
```
```
# ip route show table interconnect
35.203.0.0/18 via 10.10.0.1 dev eth0 proto bgp metric 100
34.102.128.0/17 via 10.10.0.1 dev eth0 proto bgp metric 100
```
marta: net-oncall, I recommend we 1) apply dampening for the flapping prefixes (suppress for 60s) 2) announce prepended AS path for eu-west2 to pull traffic 3) open a ticket with GCP support. Are we good to proceed?
net-oncall: proceeding with dampening and AS-path tweak now. making small changes to route-map to prefer eu-west2 for those prefixes. pushing config:
```
set as-path prepend 65001 65001
bgp dampening 60 750 2000 60
```
deploy-bot: route-map update applied to edge routers in eu-west1/eu-west2. change rolled in at 02:27 UTC.
ajay: after change, traffic shift observed: eu-west2 now receiving ~12% of private traffic for the affected prefixes. KV cache warming observed — miss rate falling to ~9% after 8m.
customer-success-bot: drafting message for AcmeCorp/Finlytics/MedData: short note + status + mitigation + ETA for full recovery. Will send after ops confirms stability.
sara: customers notified with interim update: "We detected intermittent routing instability affecting private connectivity in eu-west1. We've applied automated failover to eu-west2 and are monitoring. Next update in 30m or on change." :thumbsup:
sebastian: I'll take over the next shift in 30m. summary: flapping prefixes due to upstream GCP route churn; we dampened and shifted traffic; monitoring for re-convergence.
net-oncall: GCP Support case opened (CASE-789214) — they see repeated route withdrawals from Google side, investigating internal control-plane churn. Suggest we keep dampening for another 10m and avoid full withdraw to prevent mass re-learn.
marta: quick checks: application 99.9 latency stable on eu-west2, error rate for affected tenants down from 6.2% -> 0.8% since failover. KV-cache targets 95% warm after 18m. Good.
ajay: note: small burst of client reconnects caused a spike in tokens billed for caching operations. We'll track cost delta in the postmortem.
ops-bot: added timeline and files to INC-2026-439. tagging SRE, Network, and Support teams.
net-oncall: after 28m of monitoring, flapping subsided but GCP reports intermittent control-plane jitter. keeping AS-path prepend and dampening until 03:15 UTC.
sara: preparing post-incident customer summary template; will fill with timeline + actions and send to affected accounts once we confirm stable for 1hr.
sebastian: handoff note: I'm now primary. keep alerting thresholds same; if BGP re-flap >3 times in 10m, escalate to P1 and prepare to do full failover to eu-west2 with BGP withdraw in eu-west1.
incident-bot: Update: severity degraded to P3 at 03:02 UTC — metrics returning to baseline. Please file postmortem within 72h.
marta: agreed. I'll own the postmortem for networking cause analysis and coordinate follow-up with GCP support. I'll include KV-cache impact, customer list, cost delta, and recommended runbook updates (auto-warm caches on partial failover).
ajay: closing note: mitigations worked, but need better early-warning for interconnect jitter (extra telemetry) and an automated cache-warm path on failover.
net-oncall: closing my active ops logs; marking for watch.
sara: final customer update scheduled in 40m if no regression. thanks team. :heart:
